title: One layer model for Jest and corpus
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want one list of layers that Jest fixtures and corpus packets share, so that we do not double-count the same regex or ignore a grade we claim to care about.

## Current mess

| Surface | Layers |
| --- | --- |
| Jest fixture eval | `raw-hits`, `mentions`, `data-items`, `components`, `data-flows` |
| Corpus YAML | `components`, `data_flows`, `pii_signals`, `data_items` (no `raw_hits` packets) |
| Load path | `pii_signals` → canonical `mentions`; files may be `pii_signals.yaml` |
| Personal-data engine | `matchPiiSignalsInFiles` once; raw-hits vs mentions differ only by key prefix (`raw_hit:` vs `mention:`). Documented limitation: they are isomorphic until mentions gain a real roll-up. |

Ground-truth schema sells five grades. Corpus gold was curated as four, with `pii_signals` meaning “line-level PII signal,” which we now call mentions.

If corpus grew `raw_hits` annotations that duplicate `pii_signals` line-for-line, recall would count the same hit twice. If we never gold `raw_hits`, Jest’s extra grade is a fixture-only toy and must not be mixed into corpus headlines.

## Questions to answer

- Canonical corpus layers going forward: four (mentions not pii_signals in filenames too) or five with distinct mention roll-up?
- Rename gold files `pii_signals.yaml` → `mentions.yaml`, or keep the alias forever?
- Are raw-hits a production grade or a debug view of the same matcher?
- How do data-items (rolled-up identity-only) relate to mentions (span) so we do not treat them as independent proof of the same field?
- Initiative title is still “Four-layer scanner evaluation system” while docs say five. Which is the product?

## Not this task

Do not invent a mention roll-up algorithm here unless the decision is “mentions must differ.” Do not duplicate 325 PII records into `raw_hits.yaml`.

comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## Corpus state, measured — and the fifth grade has never existed here

Counted across all 29 packets:

| corpus layer | annotations | files on disk |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `components` | 563 | `annotations/components.yaml` |
| `data_flows` | 436 | `annotations/data_flows.yaml` |
| `data_items` | 436 | `annotations/data_items.yaml` |
| `pii_signals` | 357 | `annotations/pii_signals.yaml` |
| `raw_hits` | **0** | none |

All 29 packets use the legacy `pii_signals.yaml` filename; not one uses `mentions.yaml`. So the alias is not a transitional state, it is the only state.

### Recommendation: four grades, and rename

**Corpus is four layers. Rename `pii_signals.yaml` -> `mentions.yaml` and drop the alias** rather than keeping it forever. Reasons:

1. The alias currently costs three separate pieces of machinery: `LAYER_MAP` in `to-eval-cases.ts`, `normalizeBenchmarkLayer` + `normalizeSubjectKey` in `manifest.ts`, and a deprecated member on `BenchmarkLayer` in `schema.ts`. That is a lot of surface for a name.
2. It has already grown a fourth: `assertCanonicalSubjectKey` **hard-codes** an exemption permitting `pii:` keys on the mentions layer. All 357 mention annotations depend on it. A rename is the moment to decide whether that exemption survives (see KDATAP-d6eabf).
3. A rename is mechanical and reviewable; an alias is a permanent invitation to write `pii_signals` again.

**Raw hits are a debug view, not a production grade.** `ground-truth-schema.md` already concedes they are isomorphic to mentions — same `matchPiiSignalsInFiles`, differing only by key prefix. With zero corpus packets and no roll-up stage, the grade measures the prefix. Recommend keeping the Jest fixture cases as a matcher-level regression but **excluding raw-hits from every corpus headline**, explicitly, in the report shape. Do not gold `raw_hits.yaml`; duplicating 357 records to count the same regex twice is the failure mode the description names.

If mentions later gain a real roll-up, raw-hits gets promoted then, with its own packets. Not before.

### Data items vs mentions: not independent evidence, and the identity-only rule bites

The question *"how do data-items relate to mentions so we do not treat them as independent proof of the same field"* has a sharper answer than it looks. `hitsToDataItemFindings` builds data items **by deduplicating the same `PiiSignalHit` stream** that produces mentions. They are a `GROUP BY` over one matcher, not a second observation. Any headline that averages mention recall and data-item recall is weighting one regex twice.

Two mechanical consequences worth writing into the contract:

- `IDENTITY_ONLY_LAYERS` makes `findingMatchesCase` return true for data items with **no span check at all**, so one `data_item:email` finding anywhere in a repo satisfies every `data_item:email` gold case in that repo, in any file. Combined with the identity-only rule, data-item recall is close to a per-repo concept-coverage measure, not a localisation measure. It should be labelled as such in the report.
- Yet `isUnread` still keys data-item cases off `evidence.file_path`. So cases are dropped from the denominator based on a file that played no part in matching them. Raised on KDATAP-791091 too; it needs one answer, not two.

### Doc contradictions to resolve as part of this

- `project/wiki/four-layer-evaluation.md` is titled **"Five-grade scanner evaluation"**. The filename and the initiative (`KDATAP-f61c81dc`, "Four-layer scanner evaluation system") say four.
- `tests/eval/ground-truth-schema.md` line 3 sells five grades, and line 27 states `conceptId === ruleId` — which is false for corpus gold, where 60% of mention keys reach a rule only through `identity.ts`.

Recommend the decision here fixes the initiative title *or* the docs, in one pass, so there is a single answer to "what is the product". My vote: **four grades is the product**; five is an internal view of the personal-data matcher.

comments.text:
## Corpus state behind the four-layer decision

### Counts

| corpus layer | annotations | file on disk |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| components | 563 | `annotations/components.yaml` |
| data_flows | 436 | `annotations/data_flows.yaml` |
| data_items | 436 | `annotations/data_items.yaml` |
| `pii_signals` | 357 | `annotations/pii_signals.yaml` |
| raw_hits | **0** | none |

Two things this makes cheap:

- **Raw hits as diagnostic costs nothing to adopt.** There is no raw-hit gold to unwind and no packet to migrate. The rule is purely forward-looking.
- **The rename is a rename, not a dual-write.** All 29 packets use `pii_signals.yaml`; not one uses `mentions.yaml`. There is no split state to reconcile.

### The rename has a second surface

`normalizeSubjectKey` handles the `pii_signal:` -> `mention:` key migration, but the *keys in use* are `pii:`, and they survive via a hard-coded exemption in `assertCanonicalSubjectKey` (`tests/benchmark/manifest.ts`). All 357 mention annotations depend on it. The removal milestone must cover the `pii:` subject-key prefix as well as the `pii_signals` layer name, or the warning loader gets removed while the exemption stays. Same point on KDATAP-d6eabf.

### The data-item unit defect, in code

Confirming the "current data-item hybrid is invalid" finding with the mechanism, since the fix is two-sided:

- **Scanner side** — `hitsToDataItemFindings` in `src/eval-layers/collect-personal-data-findings.ts` collapses hits by key and keeps a **single arbitrary location**, chosen by `hit.evidence.filePath < existing.filePath` (lexicographic first). Every other supporting location is discarded. "Findings must preserve all provenance locations" is therefore a concrete change to that function, not just a schema field.
- **Gold side** — gold repeats the same repo/key across separate annotations with separate evidence, and the scorer matches identity-only with `.find()`. So one collapsed finding satisfies all of them.

Both halves have to land together; fixing only the gold consolidation while the finding still carries one lexicographically-chosen location would make evidence-strength matching arbitrary.

### Mentions and data items as related views

Supporting the "never averaged or summed as independent proof" rule with the mechanism: `collectPersonalDataFindings` derives both projections from one `matchPiiSignalsInFiles` pass over one `ingestFileSystem` result. Data items are a `GROUP BY` over the mention stream, not a second observation. Any cross-layer scalar would weight one regex twice — which is also the strongest argument for the four-layer vector over an overall percentage.

### Docs still contradict the decision

- `project/wiki/four-layer-evaluation.md` is titled **"Five-grade scanner evaluation"**; the filename and the parent initiative (`KDATAP-f61c81dc`, "Four-layer scanner evaluation system") say four.
- `tests/eval/ground-truth-schema.md` line 3 sells five grades; line 27 asserts `conceptId === ruleId`, which the corpus contradicts — only 8% of mention keys equal a rule id.

One doc pass closes both and should ride with the rename.
